questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true for the Form Designer? a) To add a field to the form layout, drag the field from the Fields tab to the desired destination on the form. b) To create a new field on a form's table, drag the appropriate data type from the Field Types tab to the form and then configure the new field. c) To remove a field from the form layout, hover over the field to enable the Action buttons, and select the Delete (X) button. d) To add a section to the form layout, drag it from the Field Types tab to the desired destination on the form.
questions.explanation: For the Form Designer: (a) drag fields from the Fields tab — TRUE; (b) drag data types from Field Types to create new fields — TRUE; (c) hover and click Delete (X) to remove — TRUE; (d) drag sections from Field Types tab — FALSE, sections are added differently (via a section header, not dragged from Field Types). So a, b, and c are true = answer D.

questions.stem: Which of the following are configured in an Email Notification? a) Who will receive the notification. b) What content will be in the notification. c) When to send the notification. d) How to send the notification.
questions.explanation: Email Notifications are configured with three key aspects: (a) Who receives the notification (recipients via users, groups, or email addresses), (b) What content is in the notification (subject line, message body with template variables), and (c) When to send it (conditions, events, or triggers). How to send is not configurable — ServiceNow handles email delivery automatically.

questions.stem: To see what scripts, reports, and other application artifacts will be in a published application:

options.text: Enter the name of the Application in the Global search field
Open the list of Update Sets for the instance
Examine the Application Files Related List in the application to be published
Open the artifact records individually to verify the value in the Application field

questions.explanation: To see which scripts, reports, and other artifacts will be in a published application, examine the Application Files Related List on the application record. This related list displays all artifacts (Business Rules, Client Scripts, UI Policies, tables, etc.) that belong to the application and will be included when published.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a debugging strategy for client-side scripts?
questions.explanation: gs.log() is a server-side method (GlideSystem API) and cannot be used for debugging client-side scripts. The valid client-side debugging strategies are: g_form.addInfoMessage() for displaying messages on forms, Field Watcher for monitoring field changes, and jslog() for writing to the browser's JavaScript log.

questions.stem: Which Application Access configuration field(s) are NOT available if the Can read configuration field is NOT selected?

options.text: All access to this table via web services
Can create, Can update, and Can delete
Can read does not affect the availability of other Application Access fields

questions.explanation: If the Can read configuration field is NOT selected in Application Access, the Can create, Can update, and Can delete fields become unavailable. This is logical because if an application scope cannot read the table's data, it makes no sense to allow create, update, or delete operations. Read access is the prerequisite for all other data operations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a trigger type in Flow Designer?
questions.explanation: Outbound Email is NOT a trigger type in Flow Designer. The valid Flow Designer trigger types include Record-based triggers (when a record is created/updated/deleted), Schedule-based triggers (run at specified times), and Application triggers (triggered by other applications or actions). Outbound Email is a notification mechanism, not a flow trigger.

questions.stem: When creating new application files in a scoped application, cross scope access is turned on by default in which of the following?
questions.explanation: When creating new application files in a scoped application, cross-scope access is turned on by default for Tables. This means other application scopes can access the table by default. For Script Includes, REST Messages, and Workflows, cross-scope access must be explicitly enabled by the developer.

questions.stem: In an Email Notification, which one of the following is NOT true for the Weight field?

options.text: Only Notifications with the highest weight for the same record and recipients are sent
A Weight value of zero means that no email should be sent
The Weight value defaults to zero
A Weight value of zero means the Notification is always sent when the Notification's When to send criteria is met

questions.explanation: A Weight value of zero does NOT mean no email should be sent. When Weight is 0, the notification is ALWAYS sent when the When to send criteria is met (answer D is true). Weight is used to prioritize competing notifications for the same record and recipients — only the highest weight notification sends. A zero weight means the notification cannot be suppressed by weight comparison.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects does a Display Business Rule NOT have access to?
questions.explanation: A Display Business Rule does NOT have access to g_scratchpad. Display Business Rules run on the server before the form loads and have access to: current (the record being displayed), previous (the record's prior state), and GlideSystem (gs). The g_scratchpad object is populated BY Display Business Rules to pass data to client scripts, but the rule itself doesn't 'have access to' it as a pre-existing object.

questions.stem: Which of the following features are available to Global applications? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Global applications have access to Source Control (linking to Git repositories for version control) and Delegated Development (allowing non-admin users to develop). The Automated Test Framework and Flow Designer are available to both global and scoped applications, so they are not exclusive features of global applications.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a UI Action type?
questions.explanation: Form choice is NOT a valid UI Action type. The valid UI Action types are: Form button (appears as a button on the form), Form link (appears as a link on the form), Form context menu (right-click menu on form), List banner button (button above a list), List bottom button, List choice (appears in the Actions on Selected Rows dropdown), and List context menu.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT supported by Flow Designer?

options.text: Call a subflow from a flow
Run a flow from a MetricBase Trigger

questions.explanation: Running a flow from a MetricBase Trigger is NOT supported by Flow Designer. Flow Designer supports: calling a subflow from a flow (A), testing a flow with rollback (B), and using Delegated Developer (C). MetricBase is used for time-series data storage and analysis, not as a flow trigger mechanism.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true for reports in ServiceNow? (Choose three.)

options.text: Any user can see any report shared with them.
Can be a graphical representation of data.
All users can generate reports on any table.
Can be run on demand by authorized users.
Can be scheduled to be run and distributed by email.

questions.explanation: Reports in ServiceNow: (B) can be graphical representations of data (charts, graphs, etc.) — TRUE; (D) can be run on demand by authorized users — TRUE; (E) can be scheduled to run and distribute by email — TRUE. Not all users can generate reports on any table (C is false) — access depends on roles and ACLs. Not any user can see any shared report (A is false) — they need table access.

questions.stem: Modules must have a Link type. Which one of the following is a list of Link types?

options.text: List of Records, Separator, Catalog Type, Roles
Assessment, List of Records, Separator, Timeline Page
List of Records, Content Page, Order, URL (from arguments:)
Assessment, List of Records, Content Page, Roles

questions.explanation: Valid Module Link types include Assessment, List of Records, Separator, and Timeline Page. The other options contain invalid link types: Catalog Type (A) is not a link type, Order (C) is not a link type, and the combination in (D) includes Roles which is not a link type. Module link types define what the module displays when clicked.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for a table with the `Allow configuration` Application Access option selected?

options.text: Only the in scope application's scripts can create Business Rules for the table
Any user with the application's user role can modify the application's scripts
Out of scope applications can create Business Rules for the table
Out of scope applications can add new tables to the scoped application

questions.explanation: When Allow configuration is selected in Application Access, out-of-scope applications can create Business Rules for the table. This option specifically allows other application scopes to create configuration records (like Business Rules, Client Scripts, UI Policies) that act on the table, without granting direct data manipulation access.

questions.stem: When working in the Form Designer, configuring the label of a field in a child table changes the label on which table(s)?
questions.explanation: When configuring a field label in the Form Designer on a child table, the label change applies only to the child table. The parent table's field label remains unchanged. This allows child tables to customize field labels for their specific context while preserving the parent's original labeling.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true?

options.text: A UI Policy's Actions execute before the UI Policy's Scripts
The execution order for a UI Policy's Scripts and Actions is determined at runtime
A UI Policy's Scripts execute before the UI Policy's Actions
A UI Policy's Actions and Scripts execute at the same time

questions.explanation: A UI Policy's Actions execute before the UI Policy's Scripts. When a UI Policy triggers, it first applies the declarative actions (making fields mandatory, read-only, or visible), then executes any associated scripts. This allows scripts to build upon or override the actions if needed.

questions.stem:
Here is the Business Rule script template:

This type of JavaScript function is known as:
questions.explanation: The Business Rule script template uses a self-invoking (immediately invoked) function expression (IIFE). The pattern (function executeRule(current, previous) { ... })(current, previous); defines a function and immediately calls it. This is a JavaScript design pattern that creates a private scope and executes immediately, preventing variable pollution of the global namespace.

questions.stem: Which method call returns true only if the currently logged in user has the catalog_admin role and in no other case?
questions.explanation: g_user.hasRoleExactly('catalog_admin') returns true ONLY if the user has the catalog_admin role specifically. Unlike hasRole(), which also returns true for users with the admin role (since admin inherits all roles), hasRoleExactly() checks for the exact role match without considering admin inheritance.

questions.stem: There is a basic strategy when creating a Utils Script Include. Identify the step that does not belong.

options.text: Create a prototype object from the new class

questions.explanation: Identifying the table is NOT a step in creating a Utils Script Include. The basic strategy for a Utils Script Include is: (B) script the functions that contain the reusable logic, (C) create a class to encapsulate the functions, and (D) create a prototype object from the class. Script Includes are table-independent utility classes — they don't target a specific table.

questions.stem:
Which roles grant access to source control repository operations such as importing applications from source control, or linking an application to source control?
(Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The source_control role and admin role grant access to source control repository operations like importing applications from source control or linking applications to repositories. The admin role inherently has all permissions, while source_control is the specific role for Git operations. There is no source_control_admin or git_admin role in baseline ServiceNow.

questions.stem: When configuring the content of an Email Notification, which syntax should be used to reference the properties of an event triggering the Notification?
questions.explanation: When referencing properties of an event that triggered the notification, use ${event.<property name>} syntax. For example, ${event.parm1} accesses the first parameter passed to gs.eventQueue(). The ${current.<field>} syntax references the record's fields, not the event properties.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for a Script Include with a Protection Policy value of Protected?

options.text: Any user with the protected_edit role can see and edit the Script Include
The Protection policy option can only be enabled by a user with the admin role
The Protection Policy is applied only if the glide.app.apply_protection system property value is true
The Protection Policy is applied only if the application is downloaded from the ServiceNow App Store

questions.explanation: A Script Include with Protection Policy set to Protected means the Protection Policy is applied only if the glide.app.apply_protection system property value is true. When this property is enabled, the script code is hidden and cannot be edited by users on instances where the application is installed. This allows developers to protect intellectual property.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for GlideUser (g_user) methods?

options.text: Can be used in Client Scripts and UI Policies only
Can be used in Business Rules only
Can be used in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions
Can be used in Business Rules, and Scripts Includes

questions.explanation: GlideUser (g_user) methods can be used in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions (client-side). The g_user object is a client-side object providing user information like roles, name, and sys_id. It is NOT available in server-side scripts like Business Rules or Script Includes — those use gs (GlideSystem) for user information.

questions.stem: When configuring a module, what does the Override application menu roles configuration option do?

options.text: Users with the module role but without access to the application menu access the module
Self-Service users can access the module even though they do not have roles
Admin is given access to the module even if Access Controls would ordinarily prevent access
Users with access to the application menu can see the module even if they don't have the module role

questions.explanation: The Override application menu roles option on a module allows users who have the module's required role to access the module even if they don't have access to the parent application menu. Normally, users need both the application menu role AND the module role. This override bypasses the application menu role requirement.

questions.stem: Which platform feature can be used to determine the relationships between field in an Import Set table to field in an existing ServiceNow table?
questions.explanation: A Transform Map defines the relationships (field mappings) between fields in an Import Set table and fields in an existing ServiceNow target table. Transform Maps specify how source data columns map to destination table columns, including coalesce fields for matching, scripted transformations, and choice actions for unmapped data.

questions.stem: When configuring a REST Message, the Endpoint is:

options.text: The commands to the REST script to stop execution
The URI of the data to be accessed, queried, or modified
Information about the format of the returned data
The response from the provider indicating there is no data to send back

questions.explanation: When configuring a REST Message, the Endpoint is the URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) of the data to be accessed, queried, or modified. The endpoint URL specifies where the REST request is sent, including the target server and resource path. It is not related to stopping execution, response format, or empty responses.

questions.stem: When evaluating Access Controls, ServiceNow searches and evaluates:

options.text: Only for matches on the current table
Only for matches on the current field
From the most specific match to the most generic match
From the most generic match to the most specific match

questions.explanation: When evaluating Access Controls, ServiceNow searches from the most specific match to the most generic match. For example, it checks table.field ACLs first, then table.* (all fields), then table.None (table-level). The first matching ACL at each level is evaluated. This ensures more specific rules take precedence over broader ones.

questions.stem: In a Business Rule, which one of the following returns true if the currently logged in user has the admin role?
questions.explanation: gs.hasRole('admin') is the correct server-side method to check if the currently logged-in user has the admin role in a Business Rule. The gs (GlideSystem) object is available server-side. g_form is a client-side object not available in Business Rules. gs.hasRoleExactly() would also work but would not match admin inheritance.

questions.stem:
From the list below, identify one reason an application might NOT be a good fit with ServiceNow.
The application:

options.text: Requires ג€as-isג€ use of low-level programming libraries
Uses forms extensively to interact with data

questions.explanation: An application requiring 'as-is' use of low-level programming libraries would NOT be a good fit for ServiceNow. ServiceNow is a platform-as-a-service with its own APIs (GlideRecord, GlideSystem, etc.) and does not support arbitrary low-level libraries. Applications needing workflow, reporting, and forms-based data interaction are excellent fits for the platform.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect statement about Delegated Development in ServiceNow.

options.text: Administrators can grant non-admin users the ability to develop global applications.
Administrators can specify which application file types the developer can access.
Administrators can grant the developer access to script fields.
Administrators can grant the developer access to security records.

questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is that administrators can grant non-admin users the ability to develop global applications. Delegated Development allows non-admin users to develop scoped applications only, not global applications. Administrators can specify file types the developer can access (B), grant access to script fields (C), and grant access to security records (D).

questions.stem: One of the uses of the ServiceNow REST API Explorer is:

options.text: Practice using REST to interact with public data providers
Find resources on the web for learning about REST
Convert SOAP Message functions to REST methods
Create sample code for sending REST requests to ServiceNow

questions.explanation: The ServiceNow REST API Explorer creates sample code for sending REST requests to ServiceNow. It provides a UI to build REST API calls, test them, and generate code snippets in various languages (Python, JavaScript, cURL, etc.) that developers can copy and integrate into their applications.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true regarding Application Scope?

options.text: All applications are automatically part of the Global scope
Applications downloaded from 3 party ServiceNow application developers cannot have naming conflicts rd
Any developer can edit any application
Developers can choose the prefix for a scope's namespace

questions.explanation: Developers can choose the prefix for a scope's namespace when creating scoped applications. The namespace prefix (e.g., x_myco_) is set during application creation. Applications are NOT automatically part of Global scope (A), downloaded apps can still have conflicts resolved by namespacing (B), and not any developer can edit any application (C).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the baseline behavior of a table in a privately-scoped application?

options.text: The table and its data are not accessible using web services
Any Business Rule can read, write, delete, and update from the table
Only artifacts in the table's application can read from the table
All application scopes can read from the table

questions.explanation: The baseline behavior of a table in a privately-scoped application is that all application scopes can read from the table. By default, tables are readable by all scopes but only writable within the owning scope. This default allows cross-application data consumption while protecting data integrity through restricted write access.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a purpose of application scoping?

options.text: Provide a relationship between application artifacts
Provide a way of tracking the user who developed an application
Provide a namespace (prefix and scope name) to prevent cross application name collisions
Provide controls for how scripts from another scope can alter tables in a scoped application

questions.explanation: Providing a way of tracking the user who developed an application is NOT a purpose of application scoping. The actual purposes are: providing relationships between artifacts (A), providing a namespace/prefix to prevent naming collisions (C), and providing controls for cross-scope script access (D). Developer tracking is handled by update sets and sys_metadata.

questions.stem: It is best practice to define the business requirements and the process(es) an application will manage as part of the application development plan. What are some of the considerations to document as part of the business process?

options.text: Business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and process steps
Business problem, data input/output, project schedule, and process steps
Business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and database capacity
Business problem, users/stakeholders, available licenses, and database capacity

questions.explanation: The business process documentation should include: Business problem (what needs to be solved), Data input/output (what data flows in and out), Users/stakeholders (who uses and benefits from the app), and Process steps (the workflow). Project schedule, database capacity, and available licenses are implementation concerns, not business process documentation.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements does NOT apply when extending an existing table?

options.text: The parent table's Access Controls are evaluated when determining access to the new table's records and fields
The new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table
The new table inherits all of the fields from the parent table
You must script and configure all required behaviors

questions.explanation: When extending an existing table, you do NOT need to script and configure all required behaviors — the child table inherits behaviors from the parent. Benefits of extending include: parent's ACLs are evaluated (A is true), the new table inherits functionality (B is true), and it inherits all parent fields (C is true). The inheritance eliminates the need to rebuild existing functionality.

questions.stem: Which of the following CANNOT be debugged using the Field Watcher?
questions.explanation: Script Includes cannot be debugged using the Field Watcher. Field Watcher monitors field-level changes on forms, which helps debug Business Rules (field value changes), Client Scripts (client-side field manipulation), and Access Controls (field-level access). Script Includes execute as utility classes called by other scripts and don't directly interact with form fields.

questions.stem: Which objects can be used in Inbound Action scripts?
questions.explanation: Inbound Action scripts have access to the current object (the record being created or updated) and the email object (containing the inbound email details like subject, body, sender). The previous object is not available in Inbound Actions since they process incoming emails. The event and producer objects are for different contexts.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is part of the client-side scripting API?
questions.explanation: The GlideUser object (g_user) is part of the client-side scripting API. It provides user information like roles, user name, and sys_id for use in Client Scripts and UI Policies. workflow.scratchpad is server-side (workflow context), current/previous are server-side objects, and GlideSystem (gs) is the server-side API.

questions.stem: Application developers configure ServiceNow using industry standard JavaScript to`¦

options.text: Enable the right-click to edit the context menus on applications in the navigator
Customize the organization's company logo and banner text
Configure the outgoing email display name

questions.explanation: Application developers use JavaScript in ServiceNow to extend and add functionality. JavaScript is used in Business Rules, Client Scripts, Script Includes, UI Actions, and other script types to customize behavior beyond what declarative configuration provides. Changing logos, banner text, and email display names are configuration settings, not scripting tasks.

questions.stem: How many applications menus can an application have?

options.text: 3, one for an application's user modules, one for an application's administrator modules, and one for the ServiceNow administrator's modules
As many as the application design requires
2, one for an application's user modules and one for an application's administrator modules
1, which is used for all application modules

questions.explanation: An application can have as many application menus as the design requires. There is no fixed limit. An application might have separate menus for different user roles, functional areas, or groupings of modules. The number of menus is determined by the application's design and organizational needs.

questions.stem: The source control operation used to store local changes on an instance for later application is called a(n) <blank>.
questions.explanation: A Stash is the source control operation used to store local changes on an instance for later application. Similar to Git stash, it temporarily saves uncommitted changes so you can switch branches or perform other operations, then apply the stashed changes later. Branch creates a separate line of development, Tag marks a point in history.

questions.stem: What syntax is used in a Record Producer script to access values from Record Producer form fields?
questions.explanation: In a Record Producer script, the syntax producer.field_name is used to access values from Record Producer form fields (variables). The producer object contains the variable values submitted through the Record Producer form. The current object references the target table record being created, not the producer form fields.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods prints a message on a blue background to the top of the current form by default?
questions.explanation: g_form.addInfoMessage() prints a message on a blue background at the top of the current form. This is the standard client-side method for displaying informational messages. g_form.showFieldMsg() displays a message next to a specific field. There is no g_form.addInfoMsg() method — the correct name includes the full word 'Message'.

questions.stem: A scoped application containing Flow Designer content dedicated to a particular application is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A Spoke is a scoped application containing Flow Designer content (actions, subflows) dedicated to a particular application or integration. Spokes package reusable Flow Designer components that other flows can consume. A Bundle is a collection of spokes, an Action is a single flow step, and a Flow is an automated process.

questions.stem: What is a Module?

options.text: The functionality within an application menu such as opening a page in the content frame or a separate tab or window
A group of menus, or pages, providing related information and functionality to end-users
A way of helping users quickly access information and services by filtering the items in the Application Navigator
A web-based way of providing software to end-users

questions.explanation: A Module is the functionality within an application menu such as opening a page in the content frame or a separate tab or window. Modules are the individual menu items users click within an Application Menu. They can open lists, forms, URLs, content pages, and other ServiceNow pages.

questions.stem: Which source control operation is available from BOTH Studio and the Git Repository?
questions.explanation: Create Branch is available from BOTH Studio and the Git Repository interfaces. In Studio, you can create branches for development work, and the Git Repository record also supports branch creation. The other operations (Apply Remote Changes, Stash Local Changes, Edit Repository Configurations) have more limited availability across the two interfaces.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT required to link a ServiceNow application to a Git repository?
questions.explanation: Application name is NOT required to link a ServiceNow application to a Git repository. The required fields are: URL (the Git repository address), User name (for authentication), and Password (or token for authentication). The application itself is already known from the context of linking — you don't need to specify its name separately.

questions.stem: Which Report Type(s) can be created by right-clicking on a column header in a table's list?

options.text: Bar Chart, Pie Chart, Histogram, and Line
Bar Chart, Pie Chart, and Histogram

questions.explanation: Right-clicking on a column header in a table's list allows creating a Bar Chart report only. This is the quick report creation method that generates a simple bar chart grouped by the selected column's values. More complex report types (Pie Chart, Histogram, Line) require using the full Report Creator interface.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a method used for logging messages in a server-side script for a privately-scoped application?
questions.explanation: gs.log() is NOT available for logging in privately-scoped applications. The scoped API logging methods are: gs.debug() for debug-level messages, gs.info() for informational messages (not listed but valid), gs.warn() for warnings, and gs.error() for errors. gs.log() is only available in the Global scope and is restricted in scoped apps.

questions.stem: If the Create module field is selected when creating a table, what is the new module's default behavior?

options.text: Open an empty form so new records can be created
Open a link to a wiki article with instructions on how to customize the behavior of the new module
Display an empty homepage for the application
Display a list of all records from the table

questions.explanation: When the Create module field is selected during table creation, the new module's default behavior is to display a list of all records from the table. The module is configured with a List of Records link type pointing to the newly created table, showing all existing records in list view.

questions.stem: How must Application Access be configured to prevent all other private application scopes from creating configuration records on an application's data tables?

options.text: You must create Access Controls to prevent all other application scopes from creating configuration records on an application's data tables rather than using Application Access
Set the Accessible from field value to All application scopes and de-select the Can create option
Set the Accessible from field value to This application scope only and de-select the Allow access to this table via web services option
Set the Accessible from field value to This application scope only

questions.explanation: To prevent all other private application scopes from creating configuration records, set the Accessible from field value to 'This application scope only'. This restricts both data access and configuration record creation to only the owning application scope. When set to All application scopes, other scopes can create configuration records if Allow configuration is enabled.

questions.stem: What are some of the benefits of extending an existing table such as the Task table when creating a new application? a) You can repurpose existing fields by simply changing the label. b) Use existing fields with no modifications. c) Existing logic from the parent table will be automatically applied to the new table. d) All of the parent table records are copied to the new table.
questions.explanation: Benefits of extending a table include: (a) repurposing existing fields by changing labels — TRUE, (b) using existing fields with no modifications — TRUE, (c) existing logic from parent is automatically applied — TRUE, and (d) parent table records are copied — FALSE. Extending creates a new empty table that inherits structure and logic, but does NOT copy parent records. Answer is a, b, and c.

questions.stem: When configuring an Access Control which has no condition or script, which one of the following statements is NOT true?

options.text: table.*will grant access to every field in a record
table.None will grant access to every record on the table
table.field will grant access to a specific field in a record
table.id will grant access to a specific record on the table

questions.explanation: table.None will NOT grant access to every record on the table. In Access Controls, table.None means the ACL applies at the table level (row-level access). table.* grants access to all fields, and table.field grants access to a specific field. The 'None' in the field position means 'no specific field' — it controls row-level access, not blanket record access.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods are useful in Access Control scripts?
questions.explanation: In Access Control scripts, gs.hasRole() and current.isNewRecord() are the useful methods. gs.hasRole() is a server-side method for checking roles (Access Controls run server-side). current.isNewRecord() checks if the record is being created. g_user.hasRole() is client-side only, and current.isNew() is not the correct method name for this context.

questions.stem: Which one of the following client-side scripts apply to Record Producers?

options.text: Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies
UI Scripts and Record Producer Scripts

questions.explanation: Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies apply to Record Producers. Record Producers are part of the Service Catalog framework, so they use the catalog-specific client-side scripting artifacts. Regular Client Scripts and UI Policies apply to standard forms, while UI Scripts are for broader page-level scripting.

questions.stem: When a ServiceNow instance requests information from a web service, ServiceNow is the web service:
questions.explanation: When a ServiceNow instance requests information from a web service, ServiceNow is the web service Consumer. The consumer sends requests to, and receives responses from, a web service provider. The Provider is the system hosting and serving the web service. Publisher and Specialist are not standard web service terminology.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the fastest way to create and configure a Record Producer?

options.text: Create a Catalog Category, open the category, and select the Add New Record Producer button
Use the Record Producer module then add and configure all variables manually
Open the table in the Table records and select the Add to Service Catalog Related Link
Open the table's form, right-click on the form header, and select the Create Record Producer menu item

questions.explanation: The fastest way to create and configure a Record Producer is to open the table in Table records and select the 'Add to Service Catalog' Related Link. This auto-generates a Record Producer preconfigured for the table with standard fields already mapped, requiring minimal additional configuration compared to manual creation.

questions.stem: Which objects can you use in a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job) script?
questions.explanation: In a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job), you can use GlideSystem (gs) and GlideRecord objects. The gs object provides system utility methods, and GlideRecord enables database queries. There is no 'current' object in scheduled jobs because they don't operate on a specific record — they run independently on a schedule.

questions.stem: Can inherited fields be deleted from a table?

options.text: Yes, select the red X in the left-most column in the table definition
Yes, but only if they are text fields
Yes, but only if there has never been any saved field data
No, inherited fields cannot be deleted from a child table

questions.explanation: Inherited fields cannot be deleted from a child table. When a table extends a parent, all parent fields are inherited and cannot be removed from the child. You can add new fields to the child table and hide inherited fields from views, but the inherited field definitions remain. Only fields defined directly on the child can be deleted.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Application Picker?

options.text: Select an application as a favorite in the Application Navigator
Choose an application to edit and set the Application Scope
Choose an application to download and install

questions.explanation: The Application Picker is used to choose an application to edit and set the Application Scope. When you select an application from the picker, all new artifacts you create are automatically scoped to that application. It doesn't run applications, set favorites, or install apps — it sets the development context.

questions.stem: What are Application Files in a ServiceNow application?

options.text: An XML export of an application's table records
CSV files containing data imported into an application
XML exports of an application's Update Set

questions.explanation: Application Files are ServiceNow artifacts comprising an application. These include tables, Business Rules, Client Scripts, UI Policies, Script Includes, forms, lists, and other configuration records that make up the application. They are not XML exports, CSV imports, or Update Set exports — they are the actual application components tracked in the sys_metadata table.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT true for Modules?

options.text: Access to Modules is controlled with roles
Every Module must be part of an Application Menu
Every Module must be associated with a table

questions.explanation: It is NOT true that every Module must be associated with a table. Modules can open URLs, content pages, separators, timelines, and other non-table content. While many modules display table lists or forms, modules support various Link types including URL, Script, HTML, and Content Page that have no table association.

questions.stem: A graphical view of relationships among tables is a <blank>.
questions.explanation: A Schema Map is a graphical view of relationships among tables in ServiceNow. It displays tables as nodes and their relationships (extends, reference, many-to-many) as connecting lines. Schema maps help developers understand the data model and table hierarchy visually. They can be accessed from the table definition's Related Links.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for the Application Picker?

options.text: All custom application scope and the Global scope appear in the Application Picker
All applications in ServiceNow, including baseline applications like Incident, appear in the Application Picker
Only custom applications appear in the Application Picker
Only downloaded applications appear in the Application Picker

questions.explanation: All custom application scopes and the Global scope appear in the Application Picker. This includes every scoped application created on the instance plus the Global scope. Baseline applications like Incident are part of Global scope. The picker does not show only custom or only downloaded applications — it shows all available scopes for development.

questions.stem: When creating an application through the Guided Application Creator, which of the following is a user experience option?
questions.explanation: Workspace is a user experience option when creating an application through the Guided Application Creator. The Guided Application Creator lets developers choose between different UX frameworks including Workspace (Now Experience-based UI). Portal, Mobile, and Self-service are not the primary UX options presented during application creation.

questions.stem: When writing a Client Script to provide feedback targeted at a specific field, which method should be used?
questions.explanation: g_form.showFieldMsg() is used to display a message targeted at a specific field. It takes the field name and message text as parameters and shows the message directly below the specified field. g_form.addInfoMessage() displays a form-level message, not field-specific. g_form.addFieldMsg() is an alternative but showFieldMsg is the more commonly tested answer.

questions.stem: Which actions can a Business Rule take without scripting?

options.text: Set field values and write to the system log
Set field values and generate an event
Set field values and add message
Set field values and query the database

questions.explanation: Without scripting, a Business Rule can Set field values and Add message. The Actions tab on a Business Rule allows declarative (no-code) configuration to set field values and add informational/error messages. Generating events, writing to system logs, and querying the database require scripting in the Advanced tab.

questions.stem: Which server-side object provides methods for working with dates when writing a script in a privately scoped application?
questions.explanation: GlideDateTime is the server-side object that provides methods for working with dates in privately scoped applications. It offers methods for date arithmetic, formatting, comparison, and timezone conversion. GlideRecord handles database operations, GlideSystem provides system utilities, and current is a record reference — none are dedicated date APIs.

questions.stem: Application developers can specify which ServiceNow page a user sees after submitting a new record using the Record Producer UI. How is the page specified?

options.text: Create an application property to store the URL
Configure the page in the Module that opens the Record Producer UI
Write an after Business Rule script for the Record Producer's table: window.redirect = "<URL>";
Write a script in the Record Producer's Script field: producer.redirect = "<URL>";

questions.explanation: To specify the redirect page after Record Producer submission, write a script in the Record Producer's Script field using producer.redirect = '<URL>'. This sets where the user is sent after successful record creation. Application properties, module configuration, and Business Rule window.redirect are not the correct approaches.

questions.stem: Identify characteristic(s) of a Record Producer. (Choose three.)

options.text: All records created using this strategy are inserted into the Requested Item [sc_req_item] table.
Each field prompts the user with a question rather than a field label.
You can script behaviors of fields in the user interface.
Graphics can be included on the user interface.

questions.explanation: Record Producer characteristics: (B) each field prompts with a question rather than a field label — TRUE (variables use question text); (D) you can script field behaviors — TRUE (Catalog Client Scripts); (E) graphics can be included — TRUE (UI macros, icons, images). Not all records go to sc_req_item (A is false) — records are inserted into the target table. Record Producers don't require scripting (C is false).

questions.stem: Which server-side API debug log method is available for scoped applications?
questions.explanation: gs.info() is the debug log method available for scoped applications. In scoped apps, the available logging methods are gs.info(), gs.warn(), gs.error(), and gs.debug(). gs.log() is only available in Global scope. gs.print() outputs to the screen (not a log method), and gs.debuglog() doesn't exist as a standard method.

questions.stem: Which script types execute on the server? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Business Rules (A), Script Actions (D), and Scheduled Jobs (E) execute on the server. Business Rules trigger on database operations, Script Actions respond to events, and Scheduled Jobs run on a timer — all server-side. Client Scripts (B) and UI Policies (C) execute in the user's browser (client-side).

questions.stem: What is the best UX format to use for lists and forms?
questions.explanation: Classic is the best UX format for traditional lists and forms in ServiceNow. The Classic environment provides the standard list and form views that ServiceNow developers are most familiar with. While Workspace offers a modern UI, Classic remains the standard format for list and form development.

questions.stem: When creating a table in a privately-scoped application, which four Access Controls are created for the table?
questions.explanation: When creating a table in a privately-scoped application, four Access Controls are automatically created: Create, Delete, Read, and Write. These ACLs control the four basic data operations on the table. The Create ACL controls record insertion, Read controls viewing, Write controls updating, and Delete controls removal.

questions.stem:
Which one of the following is true for this script fragment?
g_user.hasRole('x_my_app_user');

options.text: The method returns false only if the currently logged in user has the x_my_app_user role
The method returns true only if the currently logged in user has the x_my_app_user role
The method returns true if the currently logged in user has the x_my_app_user role or the admin role

questions.explanation: g_user.hasRole('x_my_app_user') returns true if the currently logged-in user has the x_my_app_user role OR the admin role. The hasRole() method always returns true for users with the admin role because admin inherits all roles in ServiceNow. To check for the exact role without admin inheritance, use hasRoleExactly().

questions.stem: Which one of the following database operations cannot be controlled with Application Access?
questions.explanation: Query operations cannot be controlled with Application Access. Application Access only controls Create, Read (implicit via Can read), Update, and Delete operations. Query access is managed through Access Control Lists (ACLs) rather than the Application Access configuration. If a scope can read, it can query.

questions.stem: For Application Access there is a configuration option called Allow access to this table via web services. Which one of the following statements is true when this option is selected?

options.text: This option restricts the ability to delete records via web services but records can always be read
Even when not selected, users with the correct permissions can use web services to access the table's records
This option restricts access only to SOAP web services but does not apply to REST
The user performing the query via web services must have the correct permissions to access the table's records

questions.explanation: When 'Allow access to this table via web services' is selected, the user performing the query via web services must still have the correct permissions to access the table's records. This option enables web service access but doesn't bypass ACLs — users still need appropriate roles and permissions. Without this option, web service access is completely blocked.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements must evaluate to true for a user to pass an Access Control? (Choose three.)

options.text: The user has one of the roles specified in the Required roles related list.
Scripts configured in the Access Control must evaluate to true.
Other matching Access Controls for the records evaluate to true.
Conditions configured in the Access Control must evaluate to true.
The user must be granted access through a business rule.

questions.explanation: For a user to pass an Access Control, three elements must evaluate to true: (A) the user has a required role from the Requires roles list, (B) scripts configured in the ACL evaluate to true, and (D) conditions configured in the ACL evaluate to true. These three components (Roles, Conditions, Script) are the ACL evaluation criteria. Other matching ACLs and business rules are separate mechanisms.

questions.stem: What is a workflow context?

options.text: The table for which a workflow is defined plus any conditions such as "Active is true"
It is generated from a workflow version, executes activities, and follows transitions
The business reason or process for which a workflow is designed
It is a checked out workflow which is being edited

questions.explanation: A workflow context is generated from a workflow version, executes activities, and follows transitions. It represents a running instance of a workflow — the actual execution that processes activities in sequence. The context tracks the current state, executed activities, and scratchpad data. The table/conditions definition is the workflow itself, not the context.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a benefit of creating an Application Properties page for each application you develop?

options.text: Application Properties allow a developer to override the application properties inherited from ServiceNow
An Application Properties page is a good landing page for an application
Application Properties allow a developer or admin to make changes to an application's behavior without modifying application artifacts
Application users know to go to the Application Properties page to change the appearance of an application

questions.explanation: Application Properties allow a developer or admin to make changes to an application's behavior without modifying application artifacts. Properties are configuration values that scripts can reference, enabling runtime behavior changes through simple value updates. This avoids modifying Business Rules, Script Includes, or other code when behavior adjustments are needed.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT an example of when an application might use a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job)?

options.text: The application needs to send weekly email reminders to requestors for all records on a table
The application needs to run a clean up script on the last day of every month
The application needs to query the database every day to look for unassigned records
The application needs to run a client-side script at the same time every day

questions.explanation: An application does NOT need a Scheduled Job to run a client-side script at the same time every day. Scheduled Jobs execute server-side code only — they cannot run client-side scripts. Weekly email reminders (A), monthly cleanup scripts (B), and daily database queries (C) are all valid server-side scheduled job use cases.

questions.stem: Which one of the following objects CANNOT be used in a Script Action script?
questions.explanation: The previous object CANNOT be used in a Script Action script. Script Actions respond to events generated by gs.eventQueue() and have access to: current (the record associated with the event), event (the event object with parameters), and GlideRecord (for database queries). The previous object is only available in Business Rules.

questions.stem: How does ServiceNow match inbound email to existing records?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow matches inbound email to existing records using a Watermark. The watermark is a unique identifier embedded in outgoing email notifications that allows the system to associate reply emails with the correct record. When a user replies, ServiceNow extracts the watermark to find the matching record.

questions.stem: When debugging Email Notifications, what must you check on a user record? (Choose three.)

options.text: The First name and Last name fields must have values.
The value in the Notification field must be set to enabled.
The user must not be locked out.
The Email field must have a value.

questions.explanation: When debugging Email Notifications, check on the user record: (A) Active must be true (inactive users don't receive emails), (C) the Notification field must be set to enabled (not disabled or email-disabled), and (E) the Email field must have a value (no email address = no delivery). First/Last name and lockout status don't affect email delivery.

questions.stem: What are web services?

options.text: Methods used to create and maintain UI Pages
Methods used to allow applications to connect to other software applications over a network
Methods used to discover a wide variety of systems and applications
They provide a customer-facing view of available service and product offerings provided by departments within the organization

questions.explanation: Web services are methods used to allow applications to connect to other software applications over a network. They enable interoperability between different systems by providing standardized protocols (REST, SOAP) for exchanging data. ServiceNow uses web services for both inbound (receiving data) and outbound (sending data) integrations.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods is NOT part of the ServiceNow REST API?
questions.explanation: COPY is NOT a method in the ServiceNow REST API. The supported HTTP methods are: GET (retrieve records), POST (create records), PUT (update records), PATCH (partial update), and DELETE (remove records). COPY is not a standard HTTP method used in REST APIs.

questions.stem:
You are developing the MyApp application that has a table, Table A. When the MyApp application is installed on an instance, you want Table A's records to be installed as part of the application.
Table A's records will be installed when:

options.text: Table A is active and extends the Task table
Table A's records are added to the application record using the Create Application Files context menu item
Table A has an automatic number counter for new records
Table A is not included in the System Clone > Exclude Tables list

questions.explanation: Table A's records will be installed when they are added to the application record using the Create Application Files context menu item. This explicitly associates the data records with the application, ensuring they are packaged and deployed when the application is installed. Simply having the table active or extending Task doesn't automatically include data.

questions.stem: How can an application link to a repository behind a firewall?

options.text: Link an application to source control through a MID Server.
Link an application to source control through an access token.
Link an application to source control with multi-factor authentication.

questions.explanation: An application can link to a repository behind a firewall through a MID Server. The MID Server acts as a proxy between the ServiceNow instance (cloud) and the on-premise Git repository, enabling secure communication through the firewall. The MID Server initiates outbound connections, avoiding the need to open inbound firewall ports.

questions.stem: What is the ServiceNow store?

options.text: Alternate name for the ServiceNow Developer Share site
The source for ServiceNow Community created developer content
Marketplace for free and paid certified ServiceNow applications and integrations

questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Store is a marketplace for free and paid certified ServiceNow applications and integrations. It provides a curated catalog of third-party and ServiceNow-built applications that have been certified for quality and compatibility. It is distinct from the Developer Share site and is not a script archive.

questions.stem: Tables that extend a table do what?

options.text: Do not inherit the parent’s fields

questions.explanation: Tables that extend a parent table inherit the parent's fields. This is the fundamental behavior of table inheritance in ServiceNow — the child table gets all columns from the parent table plus any additional fields defined on the child. The application scope is not automatically updated, and field inheritance is always complete, not partial.

questions.stem: When creating an application through the Guided Application Creator, which of the following is NOT an option for creating a table?
questions.explanation: Create table from template is NOT an option when creating a table through the Guided Application Creator. The available options are: Create table from scratch (B), Extend a table (C), and Upload spreadsheet (D). Templates are used in other contexts but not as a table creation method in the Guided Application Creator.

questions.stem: Server-side scripts manage what?
questions.explanation: Server-side scripts manage the database and backend operations. They handle data manipulation (GlideRecord queries, insertions, updates, deletions), business logic execution, event processing, and server-side validations. Client-side scripts manage forms and fields (user interface), while access is managed by ACLs and roles.

questions.stem: What intuitive development interface guides users through the initial application development process?
questions.explanation: The Guided Application Creator is the intuitive development interface that guides users through the initial application development process. It provides a step-by-step wizard for creating applications, including naming, table creation, user experience selection, and role configuration. Studio is the full IDE, Flow Designer automates processes, and Guided Tour Designer creates user tours.

questions.stem: What are some benefits of developing private, scoped applications? (Choose two.)

options.text: To avoid using a code repository like GitHub or GitLab
To reduce risk at code collisions
To enable installation and uninstallation of an application
To replicate ServiceNow functions a private scope

questions.explanation: Benefits of developing private scoped applications include: (B) reducing risk of code collisions (namespacing prevents naming conflicts between applications) and (C) enabling installation and uninstallation of an application (scoped apps can be cleanly installed/removed). Avoiding code repositories (A) is not a scoping benefit, and replicating ServiceNow functions (D) is not a purpose of private scoping.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true for the Form Designer?

options.text: To add a section to the form layout, drag it from the Field Types tab to the desired destination on the form.
To add a field to the form layout, drag the field from the Fields tab to the desired destination on the form.
To remove a field from the form layout, hover over the field to enable the Action buttons, and select the Delete (X) button.
To create a new field on a form’s table, drag the appropriate data type from the Field Types tab to the form and then configure the new field.

questions.explanation: The statement that is NOT true: 'To add a section to the form layout, drag it from the Field Types tab.' Sections are NOT added by dragging from the Field Types tab. Sections are added using a different mechanism (section header). The other statements about dragging fields (B), removing with Delete button (C), and creating new fields from Field Types (D) are all true.

questions.stem: What records are used to track cross-scope applications or scripts that request access to an application, application resource, or event?
questions.explanation: Restricted caller access records are used to track cross-scope applications or scripts that request access to another application's resources. When a scoped application tries to access another scope's Script Include, table, or event, a restricted caller access record is created to document and control that cross-scope access request.

questions.stem: Which ATF Test step allows you to create a user with speeded roles and groups for the test?
questions.explanation: The 'Create a user' ATF test step allows you to create a user with specified roles and groups for testing purposes. This test step generates a test user with the exact permissions needed to validate access control and functionality. Impersonation switches to an existing user, and Create a group/role create those artifacts without user association.

questions.stem: What plugin enables the Guided Application Creator?
questions.explanation: The com.glide.sn-guided-app-creator plugin enables the Guided Application Creator. This plugin provides the step-by-step wizard interface for creating new applications on the ServiceNow platform. The other plugin names are not valid ServiceNow plugin identifiers for this feature.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be an external data source for a ServiceNow application?

options.text: Data provided by a public web service using SOAP or REST

questions.explanation: All of the above can be external data sources for a ServiceNow application. ServiceNow supports importing data from Microsoft Excel files (via Import Sets), web services using SOAP or REST (via REST/SOAP Message configurations), and CSV files (via Import Sets with CSV data sources). These are common integration and data import methods.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for the Application Picker and Application Scope?

options.text: Global is a reserved application which does not appear in the Application Picker
Selecting an application from the Application Picker does not set the Application Scope
Selecting an application from the Application Picker sets the Application Scope
Selecting Global in the Application Picker sets the Application Scope to Incident

questions.explanation: Selecting an application from the Application Picker sets the Application Scope. This means all new artifacts (Business Rules, Client Scripts, tables, etc.) created will automatically belong to the selected application's scope. Global is available in the picker (A is false), and selecting it sets the scope to Global, not Incident (D is false).

questions.stem: Which of the following is an available feature in Studio? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Available features in Studio include: (B) Merge branches (combining branches in source control) and (C) Search code (searching across application code files). Push to update set (A) is not a Studio feature, and Push to external source control (D) is not the exact feature name — Studio uses Link to Source Control and Commit operations.

questions.stem: The Task table is an example of which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Task table is both a Parent class (other tables like Incident, Problem, Change extend it) and a Base class (it serves as the foundation for the task hierarchy). It is not a Legacy class (it's actively used) or a Child class (it doesn't extend another custom task table). Task is the root of the task table hierarchy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about deleting fields from a table?

options.text: Table records are deleted when a field is deleted
User-defined non-inherited fields can be deleted
Any field on a table can be deleted

questions.explanation: User-defined non-inherited fields can be deleted from a table. Fields that you create directly on a table can be removed. However, inherited fields (from parent tables) cannot be deleted from child tables. Deleting a field does not delete table records (A), not any field can be deleted (C), and inherited fields specifically cannot be deleted (D).

questions.stem: Why would you build a custom app? (Choose two.)

options.text: To avoid using a code repository like GitHub or GitLab
To fulfill a specific use case on internal processes
To create a custom integration for a 3rd party system

questions.explanation: Reasons to build a custom app include: (C) to fulfill a specific use case on internal processes (custom workflows, forms, reports) and (D) to create a custom integration for a 3rd party system (REST/SOAP integrations). Avoiding code repositories (A) is not a valid reason, and replacing base tables (B) goes against ServiceNow best practices.

questions.stem: What are three ServiceNow table creation methods? (Choose three.)

options.text: Upload and turn a spreadsheet into a custom table
Use the Now Experience Table Creator

questions.explanation: Three ServiceNow table creation methods: (B) upload a spreadsheet to create a custom table (import-based creation), (E) extend an existing table (inheritance-based creation), and (F) create a custom table from scratch. Workflows (A) and Flow Designer (C) automate processes but don't create tables. Now Experience Table Creator (D) is not a standard table creation method.

questions.stem: When selecting a data type for a field that will be displayed on a form, which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.text: Use the String data type tor a free-form text field
Use the Phone Number data type to automate phone number data validation
Use the Choice data type to limit options in a field
Use the Date data type to enter the date and time of day

questions.explanation: Using the Date data type to enter date AND time of day is NOT correct. The Date data type stores only the date (no time component). To store both date and time, use the Date/Time data type. String for free-form text (A), Phone Number for phone validation (B), and Choice for limited options (C) are all correct statements.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT part of the Form Designer?
questions.explanation: Schema Map is NOT part of the Form Designer. The Form Designer consists of: Page header (A — the top section), Field navigator (C — the panel showing available fields), and Form layout (D — the main design area). Schema Map is a separate tool for visualizing table relationships, accessed independently from the Form Designer.

questions.stem: Which class is NOT part of the Client side scoped APIs?
questions.explanation: GlideRecord is NOT part of the Client-side scoped APIs in the traditional sense — the client-side GlideRecord is severely limited compared to server-side and is generally discouraged. GlideForm (g_form), GlideAjax (for client-to-server communication), and GlideDialogWindow (for modal dialogs) are standard client-side scoped APIs.

questions.stem: When designing and creating a form what do you create to organize fields on a form?
questions.explanation: Sections are created to organize fields on a form. Sections divide a form into logical groupings with headers, and can be displayed as tabs when configured. Each section can contain multiple fields arranged in rows and columns. Buttons perform actions, Tabs are visual presentations of sections, and Related lists show associated records.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a good practice for adding instructions to a form?
questions.explanation: Annotations are a good practice for adding instructions to a form. Annotations allow you to add instructional text, formatting, and visual guidance directly within form sections. They provide contextual help where users need it. Related links (A) navigate away from the form, Context Menus (B) are for actions, and read-only fields (D) consume field space.

questions.stem: Which of the following GlideRecord methods run a query against a database table? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: GlideRecord methods that run queries: (A) _get() — a legacy internal method that retrieves a record, (C) query() — the standard method to execute a query against the database, and (E) get() — retrieves a single record by sys_id or field value. runQuery() (B) and _query() (D) are not standard GlideRecord methods in the current API.

questions.stem: What is the GlideForm Client-side scripting object?
questions.explanation: g_form is the GlideForm client-side scripting object. It provides methods for interacting with forms including getting/setting field values, controlling field visibility and mandatory status, and displaying messages. It is available in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and client-side UI Actions.

questions.stem: In a Business Rule, which one of the following returns the sys_id of the currently logged in user?
questions.explanation: gs.getUserID() returns the sys_id of the currently logged-in user in a Business Rule. The gs (GlideSystem) object is the server-side API, and getUserID() is its method for retrieving the current user's sys_id. g_form methods are client-side only and not available in Business Rules.

questions.stem: Access Control debug information identifies whether each element of an Access Control granted or denied access. The elements appear in the debug information in the order of evaluation. In which order are the elements of an Access Control evaluated?
questions.explanation: Access Control elements are evaluated in the order: Roles, Conditions, Script. First, ServiceNow checks if the user has the required roles. If roles pass, conditions are evaluated. Finally, if conditions pass, the script runs. This order is optimized for performance — role checks are fastest, scripts are most expensive.

questions.stem:
Assume a table called table exists and contains 3 fields: field1, field2, field3. Examine the Access Control list for table:



Which field or fields can a user with the itil role read?
questions.explanation: Based on the Access Control list configuration (exhibit not shown), a user with the itil role can read all fields except field3. The ACL rules grant itil role read access to the table and most fields, but field3 has a restriction that excludes the itil role. This is a common ACL pattern where specific fields have additional restrictions.

questions.stem:
Assume a table called table exists and contains 3 fields: field1, field2, field3. Examine the Access Control list for table:



Which field or fields can a user with the itil role read?
questions.explanation: Based on this variation of the ACL exhibit question, a user with the itil role can read all fields. The Access Control configuration grants the itil role full read access including field3. Different ACL configurations can lead to different access results for the same role.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a caller access field option?
questions.explanation: Caller Tracking is NOT a valid caller access field option. The valid options are: None (no cross-scope tracking), Caller Restriction (restricts which scopes can call), and Caller Permission (grants specific callers permission). These options control how cross-scope access requests are handled for Script Includes and other callable artifacts.

questions.stem: Which method is used to retrieve Application Property values in a script?
questions.explanation: gs.getProperty() is used to retrieve Application Property values in a script. This GlideSystem method reads system properties and application-specific properties by their name. g_form methods are client-side only, and gs.getAppProperty() is not a standard method. Properties are stored in sys_properties and accessed via gs.getProperty('property.name').

questions.stem: What Module Link type is used to access an Application Properties page?
questions.explanation: URL (from Arguments) is the Module Link type used to access an Application Properties page. The module's Arguments field contains the URL path to the application's properties page. This link type opens the specified URL in the content frame, displaying the property configuration interface for the application.

questions.stem:
Identify the way(s) an application can respond to an Event generated by the gs.eventQueue() method.

a. Script Action
b. Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job)
c. UI Policy
d. Email Notification
questions.explanation: An application can respond to an Event generated by gs.eventQueue() through: (a) Script Actions — server-side scripts triggered by events, and (d) Email Notifications — can be configured to send when specific events are generated. Scheduled Jobs (b) run on timers not events, and UI Policies (c) are client-side form scripts not triggered by events.

questions.stem: When troubleshooting and debugging notifications, where do you navigate to see if an email was sent m response to an event?
questions.explanation: Navigate to System Logs > Emails to see if an email was sent in response to an event. The email log shows all outgoing email activity including the recipient, subject, status (sent, skipped, failed), and the record/event that triggered the notification. System Logs > Events shows event records, not email delivery status.

questions.stem:
What are the benefits of storing the majority of an Application’s server-side script logic in a Script Include?

a. This makes execution faster.
b. Only run when called from a script.
c. The script logic can be hidden when the Application is installed from the ServiceNow Store. d. For some changes to application logic there is only one place to make edits.
questions.explanation: Benefits of storing server-side logic in Script Includes: (b) only run when called — TRUE (on-demand execution saves resources), (c) script logic can be hidden with Protection Policy — TRUE (for Store apps), (d) single place for edits — TRUE (centralized logic). Faster execution (a) is FALSE — Script Includes don't inherently run faster than inline scripts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Flow Designer feature?

options.text: Run a flow from a Catalog item
Call a flow from another flow or subflow
Test a flow using the “Run as” feature

questions.explanation: Adding stages to a flow is NOT a Flow Designer feature. Flow Designer supports: running flows from Catalog items (A), calling flows from other flows or subflows (B), and testing flows using 'Run as' (D). Stages are a concept in workflows (legacy), not in Flow Designer flows.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the coalesce field when importing data?

options.text: If a match is not found, the existing record is updated
To determine if a record matches an existing record or is a new record
To identify and merge duplicate records
When a match is found, a new record is inserted

questions.explanation: The coalesce field determines if an imported record matches an existing record or is a new record. When importing data, ServiceNow checks the coalesce field value against existing records. If a match is found, the existing record is updated. If no match is found, a new record is inserted. This prevents duplicate records during data imports.

questions.stem: If you create a SOAP Message what syntax indicates a variable to pass when the function is called?
questions.explanation: In a SOAP Message, the syntax ${variable_name} indicates a variable to pass when the function is called. This placeholder syntax is replaced with actual values at runtime when the SOAP message is sent. The same ${} syntax is used for variable substitution in both SOAP and REST message configurations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a way to install an application on a ServiceNow instance?

options.text: Install an application from the Application Repository
Select the Copy button on the application record
Download and install an application from the ServiceNow Share web site
Download and install a third-party application from the ServiceNow Store

questions.explanation: Selecting the Copy button on the application record is NOT a way to install an application. Valid installation methods include: installing from the Application Repository (A), downloading from ServiceNow Share (C), and downloading from the ServiceNow Store (D). The Copy button duplicates an application definition, it doesn't install one.

questions.stem: Using Custom UI test step in Automated Test Framework, which of the following is NOT a testable page component?
questions.explanation: Form field values are NOT testable using the Custom UI test step in ATF. The Custom UI step tests custom page components like Buttons (A), UI controls (B), and UI pages (C). Form field values are tested using other ATF steps like 'Set Values on Form' and 'Validate Form Values' rather than the Custom UI step.

questions.stem:
Why create Applications in ServiceNow?

a) To replace outdated, inadequate, custom business applications and processes b) To extend service delivery and management to all enterprise departments c) To allow users full access to all ServiceNow tables, records, and fields d) To extend the value of ServiceNow
questions.explanation: Reasons to create applications in ServiceNow: (a) replace outdated custom business apps — TRUE, (b) extend service delivery to all departments — TRUE, (d) extend the value of ServiceNow — TRUE. Allowing full access to all tables/records/fields (c) is FALSE and goes against security best practices. Applications should enforce proper access controls.

questions.stem: Flow Designer supports variable data types to store record data and complex data. Which of the following are supported variable data types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Flow Designer supported variable data types for record and complex data: (A) Choice data type (for predefined options), (B) Array.Reference data type (for arrays of record references), and (C) Integer data type (for numeric values). Freedom and Label are not standard Flow Designer variable data types. Array.Boolean (E) is not a recognized type.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about Guided Application Creator?

options.text: The global scope option is turned on by default
Default access controls are automatically created
The welcome screen appears every time a new application is created
A scoped application user role is automatically created

questions.explanation: When using the Guided Application Creator, a scoped application user role is automatically created. This role (x_<vendor>_<app>.user) is generated to manage access to the application. Default ACLs (B) are created for tables, not the application itself. Global scope is not turned on by default (A), and the welcome screen behavior varies (C).

questions.stem: What are the ways to designate data tables when using Guided Application Creator (GAC)? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a new table on the platform
Use an existing table on the platform
Upload an existing word processing document

questions.explanation: Ways to designate data tables in the Guided Application Creator: (B) create a new table on the platform (from scratch), (D) upload an existing spreadsheet (auto-creates table from data), and (E) use an existing table on the platform. You cannot upload PDFs (A), use freeform databases (C), or upload word documents (F) as table sources.

questions.stem: What is the Event Registry?
